## The shape of it

28 letters, written right to left, no capital letters, but most letters have up to four forms: isolated, initial,
medial, final. ب alone, بـ at the start, ـبـ in the middle, ـب at the end. Textbook: Alif Baa, 3rd edition
(Brustad, Al-Batal, Al-Tonsi), working through unit 4 in January 2025.

## The six that don't connect forward

ا د ذ ر ز و. They join to the letter before them but never to the one after, which leaves those little gaps inside
words. Example: دار (house) is three separate-looking pieces. Learning these six first made reading 10x less
confusing.

## Dot families

Same skeleton, different dots:

- ب ت ث ن ي: one below, two above, three above, one above (with a different tail), two below
- ج ح خ: dot inside, nothing, dot on top
- س ش: three dots on top for sh
- ص ض / ط ظ / ع غ: the dot is the only difference

## Short vowels (harakat)

Fatha ـَ = a, kasra ـِ = i, damma ـُ = u, sukun ـْ = no vowel, shadda ـّ = double the consonant. Real texts mostly leave
them out, so you read by knowing the word. Ugh. Menus in Marrakech had none at all, see [[رحلة إلى مراكش]].

## Sun and moon letters

The article ال assimilates before "sun letters" (ت ث د ذ ر ز س ش ص ض ط ظ ل ن): الشمس = ash-shams, not al-shams.
Moon letters keep the l: القمر = al-qamar. My tutor Samira (Preply, €14 a session) makes me read 10 words a session
and pick which is which.

## Related

Comparing scripts helped: Devanagari hangs from a line, Arabic sits on one, see [[Hindi Devanagari]]. Practising
names on a philosophy note, [[ابن رشد]], was a fun stretch goal.
